summary: Boonlake is an engine-building Euro from Alexander Pfister where you flip and connect tiles on a personal hex board to automate resource chains over several eras. It's a quieter, more solitaire-feeling game than his other titles, focused on tableau optimization.
criticised: Feels drier and less thematic than Pfister's other designs like Maracaibo or Great Western Trail
Dense iconography and end-game scoring bookkeeping
Low player interaction can make it feel like solitaire at the table

interaction.kind: mostly parallel engine-building with an occasional Follow action off other players' choices
interaction.detail: Like most big Pfister-style economic euros, each player mainly develops their own tableau/board through resource chains and tile placement, with a solo mode underscoring how self-contained a game can be. The 'Follow' mechanic lets you piggyback on another player's chosen action, which is the main point of contact, but it doesn't let you take or deny what an opponent needs.
interaction.said: unknown — no strong recurring interaction-specific reputation recalled; falling back on mechanics

scoring.how_you_win: Over a fixed number of rounds players build up tiles, production, and fulfilled contracts; whoever has the highest total VP once the game ends wins.

similar: Merv: The Heart of the Silk Road
